subtitle: A Queen Between Cannons and Council

panels.shot: low-angle wide of the ramparts of Ahmednagar at dusk, cannons in silhouette, Chand Bibi standing firm against a distant Mughal camp
panels.action: Chand Bibi stands on the high stone walls of Ahmednagar Fort, cloak whipped by a Deccan wind, as Mughal tents and siege guns spread across the plains below under a darkening sky.

dialogue.text: In the winter guns of 1595, one woman—Chand Bibi—stood between Akbar’s empire and the Deccan, choosing when to fight and when to surrender land to save a city.

i18n.hi: सर्दियों १५९५ में, चाँद बीबी अकेली अड़ गईं – अकबर की सल्तनत और दक्खन के बीच, सोच–समझकर लड़ते हुए, शहर बचाने को ज़मीन भी छोड़ी।

panels.shot: slow push-in from a map-filled audience hall to Chand Bibi seated in council
panels.action: In a dim audience hall lit by oil lamps, Chand Bibi sits on a modest throne, a Deccan map spread before her as courtiers, scribes and officers stand in wary semicircle.

dialogue.text: Before Ahmednagar’s walls shook, Chand Bibi had already crossed courts and dynasties—born a Nizam Shahi princess, married into Bijapur, twice a regent in a Deccan under pressure.

i18n.hi: अहमदनगर की दीवारें हिलने से पहले ही चाँद बीबी कई दरबारों और सल्तनतों से गुज़र चुकी थीं – निज़ामशाही राजकुमारी, बीजापुर की बेगम, और दबाव में दक्खन की दो बार वज़ीरा।

panels.shot: montage-like wide, split composition showing Bijapur court on one side and Ahmednagar fort on the other
panels.action: On one side, Chand Bibi appears in Bijapur’s court beside the Adil Shahi throne; on the other, she stands in Ahmednagar glancing up at the fort’s massive gates, symbolising her movement between sultanates.

dialogue.text: Chroniclers remember her first as queen of Bijapur, holding regency in a fractious court, then returning to her natal Ahmednagar when the Nizam Shahi line faltered and child rulers needed a steady hand.

i18n.hi: तारीख़-निगार पहले उन्हें बीजापुर की मलिका मानते हैं – झगड़ालू दरबार में रीज़ेंसी संभाले, फिर निज़ामशाही नस्ल डगमगाने पर अपने मायके अहमदनगर लौटीं, जब बच्चे-बाल राज कर रहे थे।

panels.shot: bird's-eye of the Deccan plateau with arrows indicating Mughal advance from the north toward Berar and Ahmednagar
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Deccan plateau shows rivers and hill-forts; from the north, stylised columns of Mughal troops and cannons march southward, arrows pointing toward Berar and Ahmednagar.

dialogue.text: By the 1590s, Akbar’s Mughal empire pushed steadily south—Khandesh overawed, Berar targeted, the Deccan sultanates divided, each bargaining, resisting, or yielding in turn.

i18n.hi: १५९० के दशक तक अकबर की मुग़ल सल्तनत लगातार दक्षिण बढ़ती गई – ख़ानदेश झुका, बरार निशाने पर, दक्खनी सुल्तनातें आपस में बंटी, कोई सौदा करता, कोई लड़ता, कोई झुकता।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Chand Bibi listening as a trembling messenger kneels
panels.action: Inside the fort’s hall, a dust-covered messenger kneels, hands clasped, while Chand Bibi leans forward, jaw set, as if weighing hard tidings.

dialogue.text: In late 1595, word reached Ahmednagar: Prince Murad, Akbar’s son, had entered the Deccan with imperial guns, and Berar’s fate would decide more than one border.

i18n.hi: १५९५ के अंत में अहमदनगर पहुँची ख़बर: शाहज़ादा मुराद, अकबर का बेटा, शाही तोपों के साथ दक्खन में उतर चुका है, और बरार की किस्मत अब कई सरहदें तय करेगी।

panels.shot: wide shot from atop Ahmednagar’s walls showing Mughal camp and artillery lines forming
panels.action: From the high battlements, Chand Bibi looks out over a vast Mughal camp spreading like a pale sea, their heavy cannons being dragged into position toward the fort’s stout walls.

dialogue.text: Soon the plains around Ahmednagar filled with canvas and steel; imperial chroniclers boasted of discipline and artillery, Deccan chroniclers of courage and stubborn stone.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही अहमदनगर के मैदानी इलाक़े फ़ौजी तंबुओं और इस्पात से भर गए; शाही मुग़ल तारीख़ें अपनी अनुशासन और तोपों की, दक्खनी तारीख़ें अपने जिगर और पत्थर की ज़िद पर फूलीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Chand Bibi at a council table, fingers resting on a revenue register and a map of Berar
panels.action: At a low table, Chand Bibi studies a parchment map of Berar alongside thick revenue registers, her hand placed between the fertile province and the symbol of the fort.

dialogue.text: Berar was no empty marchland; it was a rich revenue province whose fields fed treasuries. To hold the fort, she had to decide how much of that wealth could be lost.

i18n.hi: बरार कोई सूना कूच इलाक़ा नहीं था; यह भरपूर आमदनी वाला सूबा था, जिसकी ज़मीनें ख़ज़ाने भरती थीं। क़िला बचाने को उसे तय करना था कितना धन–धान्य कुरबान किया जा सकता है।

panels.shot: epic mid-shot of Chand Bibi standing before officers, one hand on sword hilt, another pointing toward the walls
panels.action: Gathered officers in mixed armour and robes face Chand Bibi as she stands, one hand resting on the hilt at her waist, the other gesturing firmly toward the direction of the walls.

dialogue.speaker: chand_bibi
dialogue.text: We hold the fort. We bargain with land, not with our honour.

i18n.hi: “क़िला हमारा रहेगा। सौदा ज़मीन का होगा, इज़्ज़त का नहीं।”

panels.shot: nighttime wide of the fort under bombardment, flashes at the walls and silhouettes of defenders
panels.action: Under a starless night, flashes burst against Ahmednagar’s outer walls as Mughal cannonballs strike; defenders run along parapets while Chand Bibi watches from a higher tower, veiled hair caught in the wind.

dialogue.text: The siege that followed tested stone and spirit. Ferishta speaks of nights of bombardment, rations watched carefully, and a regent who refused to abandon her post.

i18n.hi: घेराबंदी ने पत्थर और हौसले दोनों आज़माए। फ़िरिश्ता लिखता है कि रात–रात भर गोले बरसे, राशन तौला गया, और रीजेंट ने अपना मोर्चा छोड़ने से इनकार किया।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot in a small chamber where Chand Bibi dictates a letter to a scribe
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Chand Bibi sits beside a writing desk as a turbaned scribe takes down her words on folded paper, a seal lying ready beside an inkpot.

dialogue.text: From within the besieged fort, she sent letters across the Deccan, calling on neighboring sultanates—the Adil Shahis, the Qutb Shahis—to remember common interests against imperial advance.

i18n.hi: घिरते क़िले के भीतर से उसने पूरे दक्खन में ख़त भेजे, पड़ोसी सुल्तनतों – आदिलशाही, क़ुतुबशाही – को याद दिलाया कि शाही चढ़ाई के सामने उनकी मज़बूतियाँ एक हैं।

panels.shot: contrasted split-panel feel showing, on one side, Mughal generals in a tent; on the other, Chand Bibi’s council
panels.action: Inside a Mughal command tent, Prince Murad and officers sit over their own maps; opposite, Chand Bibi debates with her commanders, the two councils mirroring each other’s tension.

dialogue.text: Abul Fazl’s Akbarnama praises imperial resolve and divine favour; Ferishta emphasizes Deccan resistance. Between those narratives lay an uneasy truth—neither side wanted endless ruin.

i18n.hi: अबुल फ़ज़्ल का ‘अकबरनामा’ शाही हिम्मत और रब की मदद का गुणगान करता है; फ़िरिश्ता दक्खनी मुक़ाबले पर ज़ोर देता है। इनके बीच की सच्चाई यह थी कि कोई भी अनंत बरबादी नहीं चाहता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chand Bibi in a diplomatic audience within the fort, receiving Mughal envoys
panels.action: In a fortified hall, Chand Bibi sits erect as Mughal envoys in fine robes stand respectfully before her, their guarded expressions belying the gravity of negotiation.

dialogue.text: In early 1596, channels opened. The Mughals needed a foothold and face; Chand Bibi needed time, solvency, and her capital intact. The talks turned on Berar.

i18n.hi: १५९६ की शुरुआत में रास्ते खुले। मुग़लों को पाँव जमाने की ज़रूरत थी और इज़्ज़त की; चाँद बीबी को वक़्त, ख़जाना और अपनी राजधानी का बचना। सारी बातचीत बरार पर टिक गई।

panels.shot: close-up on Chand Bibi’s hand pressing an official seal onto a treaty document
panels.action: A close view shows Chand Bibi’s steady hand pressing a carved seal onto a folded document, while a faint diagram of Berar’s boundaries is visible on the parchment beneath.

dialogue.text: The settlement of February 1596 ceded Berar to the Mughals. It was a fiscal and territorial sacrifice—but Ahmednagar’s fort stayed under Nizam Shahi control, its administration and throne preserved for a time.

i18n.hi: फरवरी १५९६ के समझौते में बरार मुग़लों को दे दिया गया। ये माल और ज़मीन की बड़ी कुर्बानी थी – मगर अहमदनगर का क़िला निज़ामशाही के हाथ में रहा, उसकी हुकूमत और तख़्त कुछ समय को बच गए।

panels.shot: wide of city streets inside the fort returning to activity, markets reopening under watchful soldiers
panels.action: Inside Ahmednagar, shopfronts reopen and traders move cautious goods as soldiers patrol; Chand Bibi is seen in the background on a balcony, observing the city’s return to life.

dialogue.text: After the treaty, daily life slowly rose from the dust. Grain moved again, officials recalculated revenues without Berar, and Chand Bibi balanced books as carefully as she balanced alliances.

i18n.hi: संधि के बाद रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी धीरे–धीरे राख से उठी। अनाज फिर चलने लगा, दफ़्तरों ने बरार के बिना नई आमदनियाँ जोड़ीं, और चाँद बीबी ने हिसाब–किताब उतनी ही सावधानी से मिलाए जितनी सतह पर अपनी सियासत।

panels.shot: medium shot in council showing factions arguing, with Chand Bibi between a conservative officer and a younger hothead
panels.action: In the council chamber, one grey-bearded officer leans toward caution while a younger commander gestures angrily toward the north; Chand Bibi sits between them, face marked by fatigue and resolve.

dialogue.text: Yet peace was brittle. Court factions argued—some resenting the loss of Berar’s revenues, some eager to defy the Mughals outright, others quietly favouring accommodation. The regent walked a narrowing path.

i18n.hi: फिर भी सुलह नाज़ुक थी। दरबार के गुट भिड़ गए – कुछ बरार की आमदनी जाने से खफ़ा, कुछ मुग़लों से खुली टक्कर के हामी, कुछ चुपचाप नरम रुख़ के पैरोकार। रीजेंट का रास्ता हर दिन पतला होता गया।

panels.shot: moody mid-shot of Chand Bibi alone at night, looking over correspondence by lamplight
panels.action: At night, Chand Bibi sits alone by a small lamp, unread letters and reports piled around her as shadows lengthen along the carved stone walls.

dialogue.text: Modern historians see her not as a romantic heroine on battlements, but as an early modern ruler, wrestling with paperwork, provincial finances, and the politics of a connected subcontinent.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार उन्हें किले की रोमांटिक वीर नायिका से ज़्यादा, शुरुआती आधुनिक दौर की शासक मानते हैं – जो काग़ज़ी काम, सूबों की आमदनी और जुड़े हुए उपमहाद्वीप की सियासत से जूझ रही थीं।

panels.shot: tense interior wide of armed soldiers crowding into a palace corridor in 1600, faces suspicious
panels.action: A later scene shows armed soldiers surging through a palace corridor, eyes narrowed with suspicion, as whispers seem to coil through the air toward a closed inner chamber.

dialogue.text: By 1600, imperial pressure resumed and internal divisions sharpened. In that confusion, rumours spread that Chand Bibi would surrender the fort—a claim the sources recount but cannot fully untangle.

i18n.hi: १६०० तक शाही दबाव फिर बढ़ा और अंदरूनी फूट गहरी हो गई। इस अफ़रा–तफ़री में अफ़वाह उड़ी कि चाँद बीबी क़िला सौंप देंगी – तारीख़ें इस दावे को दर्ज करती हैं, पर गांठ पूरी नहीं खोल पातीं।

panels.shot: somber mid-shot of Chand Bibi facing a group of her own men, their expressions conflicted
panels.action: Chand Bibi stands facing a group of her own soldiers in an inner courtyard, their faces a mix of anger, fear and reluctance, as if torn between loyalty and suspicion.

dialogue.text: Ferishta records that in the panic, some of her own men turned on her, convinced she would betray them. In the turmoil, the regent who had saved the fort was killed inside its heart.

i18n.hi: फ़िरिश्ता लिखता है कि भगदड़ में उनके कुछ अपने सिपाही ही उन पर टूट पड़े, यक़ीन कर बैठे कि वह उन्हें बेच देंगी। इस ही हलचल में, जिसने क़िले को बचाया था, वही रीजेंट उसके दिल में ही मारी गई।

panels.shot: high wide shot of Ahmednagar Fort, now under a new order, fading Chand Bibi’s silhouette over the walls
panels.action: A high view shows Ahmednagar Fort under a changed guard, Mughal standards and new officials moving through its gates, while a faint, translucent silhouette of Chand Bibi seems to overlook the city one last time.

dialogue.text: Her death did not halt the Mughal tide, but her stand delayed it and reshaped it. In Chand Bibi’s story, courage holds a wall, but it is her hard bargaining and clear-eyed governance that still echo in the Deccan’s history.

i18n.hi: उनकी मौत ने मुग़ल लहर नहीं रोकी, मगर उसकी रफ़्तार और रेखा बदल दी। चाँद बीबी की दास्तान में दीवारें तो जिगर ने थामीं, पर आज भी दक्खन में उनकी सख़्त सौदेबाज़ी और साफ़–नज़र हुकूमत की गूँज सुनाई देती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: A Queen Between Cannons and Council
subtitle_i18n.hi: तोपों और दरबार के बीच एक रानी
